The Addiction to Assignment initiative has launched its National Anti-Drug High School and Youth Tour, a nationwide campaign aimed at raising awareness about drug abuse and preventing substance use among young people.
The initiative, spearheaded by Timothy Bentum, draws on his personal journey from cocaine and heroin addiction to sobriety and purpose, with the aim of using lived experience, celebrity influence and public education to confront the growing drug menace among Ghana’s youth.
The tour is being undertaken in collaboration with the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) and JoyPrime TV.
Speaking at the launch, NACOC Director-General, Maj. Gen. Maxwell Obuba Mantey pledged his outfit’s full support for the initiative.
Discussions are also underway with the Ghana Education Service to facilitate the smooth implementation of the programme across schools nationwide.
The campaign will bring together personalities from the creative arts industry and other stakeholders to engage students directly on the dangers of drug abuse and the importance of making positive life choices.
Organisers are calling on government, corporate Ghana, parents and the general public to support the initiative in safeguarding the future of the next generation.
